scenario: PROOF-1 security gate vs a REAL codebase

corpus.negative: the platform's own 1657 deployed Python files
corpus.positive: 12 planted files, one danger class each, labelled by construction

recall.note: unambiguous - each plant contains exactly one danger class

improvement.cause: has_call matched '.compile(' etc; re.compile is not compile

remaining_flags_are: genuine uses of subprocess/os.system/SQL string building in a dev repo, NOT injected vulnerabilities. A lexical scanner cannot separate 'app shells out on purpose' from 'user input reaches a shell' - that needs taint analysis.
verdict: PROVEN: 12/12 recall on labelled danger, and the precision defects found by running against real code were real bugs that are now fixed (43% fewer flags). NOT PROVEN: that this is a usable automatic CI gate. At 19.6% flag rate a human cannot read every flag. The defensible use is review-highlighting - 'show me every place that shells out / deserialises / builds SQL' - which is a real question, not an automatic pass/fail.
